paper_title: OMNIGUARD An Efficient Approach for AI Safety Moderation Across   Modalities
caption: Accuracy of detecting harmful prompts in a few-shot setting. As few-shot examples are provided, quickly achieves near-perfect accuracy, despite the attacks being quite different from its training data (e.g. without any few-shot examples, 's accuracy is close to 50% ). In contrast, the guard model baselines improve their accuracy slowly in a few-shot setting, despite sometimes having seen similar code attacks in their training data. Accuracies are averaged over 50 random sets of few-shot examples; error bars show the standard error of the mean.
model_annotation:
The plot illustrates the accuracy of several models—OmniGuard, AegisGuard (P), AegisGuard (D), LlamaGuard 1, LlamaGuard 2, and DuoGuard—as a function of the number of few-shot examples provided. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Few-Shot Examples” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 5, with tick marks at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 50 to 90, with tick marks at intervals of 10. 

The OmniGuard model is represented by a black line with circle markers; starting at approximately 68 at x=0, the line increases sharply to approximately 92 at x=1, then continues increasing gradually to approximately 95 at x=5. AegisGuard (P) is shown as a blue line with square markers beginning at around 74 at x=0, reaching a peak of approximately 82 at x=1, then decreasing to about 71 at x=3, and ending at around 64 at x=5. The AegisGuard (D) model is represented by a red line with plus markers, starting at approximately 64 at x=0, decreasing to about 51 at x=1, and remaining around 52-53 from x=2 to x=5. LlamaGuard 1 appears as a yellow line with asterisk markers, beginning at around 87 at x=0 and ending at about 84 at x=5 with very little change in between. The LlamaGuard 2 data is displayed as an orange line with plus markers, beginning at approximately 88 at x=0 and reaching approximately 90 at x=1 before decreasing gradually to approximately 87 at x=5. Finally, the DuoGuard model is represented by a purple line with cross markers, starting at about 62 at x=0 and decreasing to approximately 58 at x=5. Error bars are displayed for each data point and extend vertically.
